name: CrewCue
subtitle: For ultra runners and the crews who chase them
pitch: CrewCue builds your splits to every aid station, then keeps your crew on the same page while you run: where you are, when you'll arrive, and what you need when you get there.
status: In development. No public build yet

features.title: A pace plan for the course you're running
features.text: Import the GPX and get an estimated finish with splits to each aid station, adjusted for the climbing in between.

features.title: Live position and arrival times
features.text: Your phone reports where you are. Your crew sees percent complete, the next aid station and a live ETA, with a warning if a cutoff is getting close.

features.title: Aid-station check-ins
features.text: One tap when the runner comes through, and everyone on the crew knows.

features.title: Crew chat
features.text: Messages and photos in one thread, with push notifications that respect who needs to know what.

features.title: Works when the signal doesn't
features.text: Actions queue offline and sync when the canyon lets you back on the network.

features.title: A schedule your crew can print
features.text: Export the plan as a sheet: where to be, when, and what to have ready.

engineering.intro: A native iOS and Android app sharing one Swift core, with a TypeScript API behind it. I prototyped in React Native to move fast, then directed the move to native once the product's shape was clear.

facts.v: native clients: SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose
Swift core shared by both, over JNI on Android
API test files, plus Postgres integration tests
pull requests and issues in the repository so far

points.title: One Swift core, two platforms
points.text: Business logic lives in a UI-free Swift package. iOS links it directly; Android calls it through JNI using the Swift Android SDK. Wire types for both are generated from one contracts package.

points.title: Prototype in Expo, ship native
points.text: I used Expo to get a working product quickly and learn what the app needed to be. Once maps, chat and background location became the core of it, I rebuilt the clients natively so they use the platform SDKs directly. The decision and its trade-offs are written up as an architecture decision record.

points.title: Parity you can check
points.text: Each feature has a behavior checklist and a fixture deep link, and both platforms record device proof against it. A feature isn't done until iOS and Android both pass.

points.title: An API built for bad networks
points.text: Fastify and Zod on Postgres, with an event log, snapshots and idempotency keys so a retried request from a dead zone never double-applies.

points.title: CI on every pull request
points.text: Lint, types, API and Postgres tests, an XCUITest smoke run, Android emulator tests, a Swift cross-compile for Android, CodeQL and secret scanning.

points.title: Agents merge, humans release
points.text: Agents merge their own reviewed pull requests. A guard hook stops them from tagging a release or touching production, and the production deploy waits for my approval.

try.title: Set a goal. Watch the splits move.
try.text: Drag the goal time and the plan re-paces every climb. Move the race clock to see what your crew would see mid-race.
